clue.text: Problem in pet rabbit

definitions.note: in British slang to rabbit is to talk on and on, so here it means idle talk

indicators.note: the clue says the problem sits in the pet, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: a cat is a typical household pet
a hitch is a snag or problem

explanation.surface: Someone frets over a difficulty with their pet bunny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rabbit' looks like the animal from the surface, but it is British slang for chatter and is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabbit as a noun is British slang for idle talk, which is the same as light gossipy conversation.

clue.text: Material, parts of which are in alphabetical order

definitions.text: Material, parts of which are in alphabetical order

parts.words: Material, parts of which are in alphabetical order
parts.note: the fabric's six letters, read left to right, each come later in the alphabet than the one before

explanation.surface: A fabric whose pieces have been neatly sorted from A to Z.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parts' suggests pieces of cloth, but the parts are the letters of the word: C, H, I, N, T, Z run in alphabetical order.
explanation.definitionFit: Chintz is a printed, glazed cotton fabric, so it is a material.

clue.text: Flowers one gets out of bed

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
someone who rises gets up out of bed

explanation.surface: Blooms seem to wake and climb out of their flower beds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bed' hints at a flower bed, but it is where one sleeps.
explanation.definitionFit: Irises are garden plants with showy blooms, so they are examples of flowers.

clue.text: A neurotic drunk's drink

indicators.note: drunk is used for the letters, which are reeling about and rearranged

explanation.surface: An anxious drunkard orders their tipple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' looks like a person but signals the anagram of A NEUROTIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Cointreau is an orange-flavoured French liqueur, an example of an alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: In a class of one's own?

definitions.text: In a class of one's own?

parts.words: In a class of one's own?
parts.note: unrivalled is the usual sense, but literally a class with a single pupil is someone teaching themselves

explanation.surface: A phrase praising someone as unrivalled and peerless.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom means outstanding; read literally it is a classroom of one, the self-taught learner.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone self-taught learns without a teacher, so their lessons have just one participant.

clue.text: Back a Scottish inventor with zero capital

parts.note: zero looks like the letter O

indicators.note: back tells us to read the article and the inventor's name from right to left

parts.note: James Watt, the Scottish engineer who improved the steam engine

explanation.surface: An instruction to support a Scottish inventor who has no money at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' reverses A plus WATT to make TTAWA; O for zero goes in front. 'capital' looks like money with 'zero', but it means a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Ottawa is the capital city of Canada, so it is an example of a capital.

clue.text: Roman garment in port on Med, shortened cape

indicators.note: shortened cuts the last letter off the port

parts.note: Tunis is the capital and port of Tunisia on the Mediterranean
C is the map abbreviation for cape

explanation.surface: A Roman garment is bought in a Mediterranean port along with a cropped cape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortened' looks like it trims the cape but trims Tunis to TUNI.
explanation.definitionFit: A tunic was the basic knee-length garment worn by Romans.

clue.text: A large idea-incomplete, however

parts.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

indicators.note: incomplete drops the final letter of the idea

parts.note: a thought is an idea

explanation.surface: Someone has a big but half-formed idea, though.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incomplete' trims the last T of THOUGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: As a conjunction this word means in spite of the fact that, which is also a sense of however.

clue.text: A quiet river location is fitting

parts.note: P stands for piano, the musical direction for quiet
the Po is the longest river in Italy
a site is a location

explanation.surface: A peaceful riverside spot is just right.
explanation.walkthrough: P is piano in music, meaning soft or quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: Apposite means apt or suitable, the same as fitting.

clue.text: Start succinct account of visit to restaurant?

definitions.meaning: to start something is to begin or launch it

definitions.text: succinct account of visit to restaurant?
definitions.meaning: read as three words, a terse diner's report would say they went in, then ate there

explanation.surface: A prompt to begin a short review of a meal out.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as IN IT I ATE, the answer is a four-word summary of going into a restaurant and eating; the question mark flags the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To initiate a project is to begin it, a straightforward synonym for start.

clue.text: Moving description of trained infantry? For example, Wellington's section

definitions.meaning: soldiers marching well together are said to be marching ...
a Wellington is a rubber boot, and the arched middle part of a boot or foot is its upper arch

explanation.surface: Drill-ground praise for soldiers, then a nod to the Duke of Wellington's army unit.
explanation.walkthrough: Wellington here is a wellington boot (a British rubber boot), not the Duke, so its 'section' is a part of the boot rather than a military section.
explanation.definitionFit: The arched top of the foot between toes and ankle, and the matching part of a boot, has this name.

clue.text: Marginally risky strategy showing British skater's skill?

parts.note: a playful coinage: the craft of handling oneself on an ice rink

explanation.surface: A British skater shows off a daring routine at the edge of the ice.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the invented word, rink plus -manship, as skill at the rink.
explanation.definitionFit: The policy of pushing a dangerous situation to the verge of disaster to gain an advantage.

clue.text: Message that's short, time after time

T again stands for time

explanation.walkthrough: 'short, time' gives WEE T, a short time, which comes after the other T.
explanation.definitionFit: A post on the social network once called Twitter is a short online message.

clue.text: Businessmen or others who make cuts

definitions.meaning: members of a company board running a business

explanation.walkthrough: 'cuts' suggests budget slashing beside 'Businessmen', but it is the film set's call to stop filming.
explanation.definitionFit: Board members of a company and the people in charge of a film both go by this title.

clue.text: Influential member interpreting correctly, after changing sides initially

indicators.note: the sides are right and left, so the letter for right gives way to the letter for left in the first word

parts.note: reading a situation means interpreting it

indicators.note: initially says the same right-to-left swap happens at the start of the second word too

parts.note: right means correctly, as in did it right

explanation.surface: A prominent member reads things properly after switching political parties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing sides initially' turns the R starting each of READING and RIGHT into L. The surface suggests defecting politicians.
explanation.definitionFit: A prominent, guiding figure in a group or movement is called this, an idiom for someone others follow.

clue.text: Ancestral pieces relocated in royal house

indicators.note: the word's pieces are moved to new places, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Family heirlooms are moved to a palace.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of ANCESTRAL is signalled by 'pieces relocated'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lancaster was an English dynasty of kings from Henry IV to Henry VI, so it names a royal family line.

clue.text: Cutting remarks about problem in tropical island

clue.text: Something in deal one can see through? It's incomplete, so to speak

clue.text: Proclamation in a new part of speech introducing bond

explanation.definitionFit: A public statement or declaration is a proclamation, a near synonym.

clue.text: Family doctor's put inside old Eastern robe

clue.text: Opposed to poetry recital?

clue.text: Section of army volunteers entering club before hero

clue.text: End of my weapon put back, liable to drop off
